result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A pads the measured values with invented trailing zeros (3.00, 8.000, 41.000), and its table runs past 1280px, cutting off a column. B shows the values exactly as given and fits the screen, but because it right-aligns the numbers, the decimal points don't line up (1.5 vs 0.75). Both add calculated per-foot and per-pound columns that weren't asked for, and B also adds summary cards. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A shows every measurement exactly as recorded, and its prices are consistent to two decimals. However, its measured columns are flush-right rather than aligned on the decimal point, and it adds summary cards and derived columns that weren't requested. B lines up the decimals only by padding values with invented zeros (3.00, 8.000, 41.000), which breaks the precision requirement. It also overflows the 1280px width, so its last column is cut off. Both answers add per-foot and per-pound columns that weren't asked for.
